question: CaO(s) + H₂O(I) → Ca(OH)₂(aq) + Heat, this reaction is called:
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Combination Reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A **combination reaction** is a type of chemical reaction where two or more substances combine to form a single product.
 
• In the given reaction, **CaO (calcium oxide)**, also known as quicklime, reacts with **H₂O (water)** to form **Ca(OH)₂ (calcium hydroxide)**, which is commonly known as slaked lime.
